<reflection>
The fitting results from the first experiment show that many mechanisms have very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values (around -23.3), indicating that the initial moderate-condition experiment was not highly discriminative. Only M4 and M5 are clearly worse (NLL > -10), while M3 is slightly worse. The small differences among the top group mean that we cannot yet rule out most mechanisms. The aim for this turn is to propose an experiment that provides greater discrimination, particularly among the closely ranked mechanisms, by introducing a new variable that targets specific mechanistic features.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Adding a moderate initial concentration of product (0.1 M) while keeping substrate and catalyst concentrations the same as in the first experiment isolates the effect of product on the kinetics. This condition tests for reversibility of the catalytic step and product-induced inhibition or deactivation. Mechanisms with reversible product binding (e.g., M1, M2) will exhibit a slower net forward rate due to the increased reverse reaction. Mechanisms with irreversible product deactivation (e.g., M12, M17) may show accelerated loss of catalytic activity. In contrast, mechanisms without product sensitivity (e.g., M6, M7, M8) will be largely unaffected, except possibly through reverse reactions if included. Comparing the time course with and without product will help distinguish these classes, providing information across multiple mechanisms simultaneously. This design avoids extreme conditions and introduces a new dimension (product concentration) that is directly relevant to several candidate mechanisms.
</hypothesis>
